title: John Deere launches AI assistant to analyse farm business data
description: John Deere has launched JD, a new artificial intelligence assistant designed to help farmers analyse operational data and turn information from machinery and fieldwork into practical insights. Currently available free of charge through the John Deere Operations Center web and mobile applications, JD allows users to ask questions in everyday language rather than searching manually through different data sources. The assistant uses customer-authorised information from individual farming operations, including historical field, machine and workflow data, to provide context-specific answers. Functions include analysing past operational performance, reviewing equipment and land productivity, and assessing how decisions such as fertiliser rates, cultivation intensity and variable-rate applications have affected crop yields. READ NOW: Lunar rover? Or the future of vineyard crop protection at EIMA? JD can also help users navigate John Deere software and machinery by finding relevant information in operator manuals and support guides. John Deere says the technology is designed to reduce the time farmers spend searching for information, allowing them to identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce costs and make more informed management decisions. Unlike general-purpose AI assistants, JD draws on data specific to the customer's operation rather than relying primarily on publicly available information. The manufacturer says all customer information remains within the Operations Center and is protected by the platform's existing security systems and permissions. Users retain control over their data and who it is shared with.
